neighbours.label: The surname after a formal, old-fashioned given or middle name, on its last piece or whole token ('Amasa Sprague', 'John Campbell Merriam', 'Stilson Hutchins', 'Amasa Stone'); the same surnames after a modern first name stay low.
fire: In 1871 Ebenezer Whitcomb gave land for the school.
It was endowed by Zebulon Hathaway of Vermont.
The first dean was Josiah Thornton Babcock of Yale.
Elder Hezekiah Sprague led the church for years.
The Amos Lawrence Harkness Chair was founded in 1902.
Mr. Lemuel Hutchins printed the county paper.
The map was drawn by Obadiah Merriam, surveyor.
Dr. Thaddeus Warren Orcutt wrote to the governor.
quiet: In 1871 Kevin Whitcomb gave land for the school.
It was endowed by Jason Hathaway of Vermont.
The first dean was Brian Babcock of Yale.
Elder Tyler Sprague led the church for years.
The Brandon Lawrence Harkness Chair was founded in 1902.
Mr. Kyle Hutchins printed the band's flyer.
The map was drawn by Justin Merriam, surveyor.
Dr. Dylan Warren Orcutt wrote to the governor.

short: surname after an old-fashioned given name
notes: Probes: 0.37-0.90, and whole-token 'Amasa Stone' 0.65. 'Alfred Hitchcock' 0.06 (fame may matter there), 'Mike Hutchins' 0.01, 'John Campbell Smith' 0.21, 'Thomas Moore' 0.05. This is a pattern, tested on new names; it may be about the name's rarity or about 19th-century text. I can't separate these here. Near misses change only the first name, keeping the old setting, which makes them odd on purpose.
